scenes.heading: Shuffle Optimization
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Shuffle Optimization and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: Levers that reduce shuffle cost
items: Prefer broadcast joins for small sides
Filter and pre-aggregate before the shuffle
scenes.narration: Optimizing shuffles is largely about moving less data and moving it in the right number of pieces. Tuning the shuffle partition count avoids both tiny tasks and giant ones. Broadcasting a small join side removes a shuffle entirely, while filtering and pre-aggregating upstream shrinks the volume that ever needs to move.

scenes.heading: Too few vs too many partitions
scenes.narration: Setting shuffle partitions too low creates a few huge tasks that spill to disk or run out of memory and leave cores idle. Setting it too high creates thousands of tiny tasks whose scheduling and file overhead dominates the real work. The goal is partitions large enough to amortize overhead but small enough to fit in memory, which AQE can now tune automatically.

scenes.code:
# Pre-aggregate to shrink shuffle volume
daily = (events.groupBy("day", "user").count())

# Right-size partitions (or let AQE do it)
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "400")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")

# Broadcast the small dimension instead of shuffling
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
out = daily.join(broadcast(users), "user")
scenes.heading: Stacking the optimizations
scenes.narration: First, aggregating by day and user before any join shrinks the data that must be shuffled downstream. Next, we set a sensible shuffle partition count and enable AQE so Spark can coalesce further based on real sizes. Finally, broadcasting the small users dimension removes a shuffle from the join altogether. Combining these techniques compounds the savings.

scenes.heading: A tuning workflow
steps: Find the shuffle in Spark UI
scenes.narration: A disciplined workflow starts in the Spark UI, where you locate the expensive Exchange and inspect its task sizes and any spill. If tasks are huge and spilling, add partitions or broadcast a small side; if they are tiny, coalesce. Then re-run and compare, because tuning without measurement is guesswork.

scenes.text: Move less data first, then right-size the shuffle.
scenes.narration: Predicate pushdown, pre-aggregation, and broadcasting beat any partition-count tweak because they shrink the shuffle itself.
